Q: What is Video RAM (VRAM) in common usage?
Option1: The Windows swap file on disk
Option2: Memory dedicated to graphics processing, either on a graphics card or integrated package

Q: What is Small Outline Dual Inline Memory Module (SODIMM)?
Option1: A desktop full size memory module
Option2: A smaller laptop and small form factor memory module type
Option3: A permanent chip soldered to the motherboard

Q: What is Double Data Rate 3 (DDR3) memory?
Option1: The latest desktop memory
Option2: An older DDR generation not pin compatible with DDR4 or DDR5

Q: What is Double Data Rate 4 (DDR4) memory known for versus DDR3?
Option1: Lower typical voltage and higher bandwidth; not pin compatible with DDR3
Option2: Uses the same physical notch as DDR3

Q: What is Double Data Rate 5 (DDR5) memory?
Option1: A graphics only memory
Option2: The newest mainstream DDR generation with further bandwidth and efficiency increases; not pin compatible with DDR4

Q: What does Error Correction Code (ECC) RAM provide?
Option1: Extra capacity only
Option2: Detection and correction of single bit errors to improve reliability when supported by the system

Q: Which systems typically support ECC RAM?
Option1: Most consumer laptops by default
Option2: Servers and workstations with ECC capable motherboards and processors

Q: What is 'single channel' in memory configuration?
Option1: One memory module operating on a single 64 bit bus to the controller
Option2: Two modules synchronized for double bandwidth
Option3: Four modules in parallel with error correction

Q: What is 'dual channel' memory?
Option1: Two matched modules accessed in parallel to increase memory bandwidth
Option2: One module with higher speed
Option4: Two different capacities in any slots with no effect

Q: What is 'triple channel' memory?
Option1: Three unrelated modules in any slots
Option2: Three modules accessed in parallel on platforms that support it

Q: What is 'quad channel' memory?
Option1: Four channels used in parallel on supported platforms to increase bandwidth
Option2: Four random sticks in any board

Q: When installing RAM, what is the most important physical alignment check?
Option1: Keyed notch on the module must match the slot to avoid damage
Option2: Heatsink size

Q: A desktop supports dual channel and has four slots labeled A1 A2 B1 B2. Which population enables dual channel with 2 sticks?
Option1: Install both in A1 and A2
Option2: Install in A1 and B1 or follow the manual for matching colored slots
Option3: Install in any two slots randomly
Option4: Install in B1 and B2 only

Q: A laptop requires more memory and uses SODIMM DDR4. Which statement is correct?
Option1: Any DDR3 SODIMM will also work
Option2: Use DDR4 SODIMM modules that match the specification; DDR3 will not fit or operate
Option3: Use desktop DIMMs for better performance

Q: Mixing ECC and non ECC in most boards that support ECC will result in what?
Option1: ECC always enabled
Option2: Usually a boot failure or ECC disabled depending on the board; mixing is not recommended

Q: What is 'virtual memory' on a desktop?
Option1: Extra physical memory modules
Option2: Disk space used as temporary memory when physical RAM is insufficient

Q: A system powers on but repeatedly beeps and shows no display after a RAM upgrade. First best step?
Option1: Force the modules in harder
Option2: Remove and reseat modules, verify the correct type and notch alignment, and test one at a time
Option4: Clear the CMOS immediately without checks

Q: Which statement about RAM speed is correct?
Option1: Higher rated speed always runs at that speed automatically
Option2: Module speed is limited by the slowest module and the motherboard capability
Option3: Speed is determined only by the CPU fan

Q: You must maximize throughput on a workstation that supports quad channel operation. Best practice?
Option1: Install one very large module
Option2: Install four identical modules in the correct color coded slots for quad channel
Option3: Mix different sizes across any slots

Q: A board lists support for DDR5 non ECC only. Which RAM will fit and function?
Option1: DDR4 ECC
Option2: DDR5 non ECC DIMMs of supported speed
